title: Community Impact Grants: Spring Cycle
summary: Unrestricted general operating support for nonprofits working in health, human services, and civic and economic opportunity across Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, and Apache counties.
description: The Spring Cycle of the Community Impact Grants program provides one-year, unrestricted general operating support to organizations meeting basic needs and expanding economic opportunity in northern Arizona. Unrestricted funding lets organizations put dollars where they are needed most, whether that is staff salaries, rent, or a new program.

Award amounts are set by the applicant's annual operating budget, so organizations do not need to request a specific amount. The Foundation expects to award approximately $650,000 to 45 to 55 organizations in the 2027 Spring Cycle.
impact_areas: Affordable and supportive housing and homelessness prevention
Access to primary, dental, and behavioral health care
Services for older adults and caregivers
Safety and services for survivors of violence
Workforce training and support for hourly and seasonal workers
Financial coaching, benefits access, and small business development
Civic engagement, open government, and access to justice
populations_served: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness

geography.summary: Organizations must be located in or provide services to residents of Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties, Arizona.

eligibility: Tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, a public or governmental agency, a federally recognized tribe or tribal program, or a project with a qualified fiscal sponsor
Located in or primarily serving residents of Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties
In operation for at least two years with a board-approved annual budget
Non-discriminatory in hiring, board membership, and delivery of services
Work aligns with at least one Spring Cycle field of interest: Health & Human Services or Civic & Economic Opportunity
One Community Impact Grant application per organization per calendar year (Spring or Fall, not both)
not_eligible: Organizations that received a Community Impact Grant in calendar year 2026 (recipients of donor-advised grants remain eligible)
Religious activities, although faith-based organizations providing secular services to all are eligible
Capital campaigns, endowments, or debt reduction

funding.summary: $5,000 to $25,000, determined by the organization's annual operating budget

dates.info_session: Applicant information session (virtual): Thursday, February 4, 2027, 10:00 a.m. MST

how_to_apply.intro: Applications are submitted through the CPCF Grant Portal. Review the guidelines and use the application worksheet to prepare your answers before you begin.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility
steps.text: Review the 2027 Spring Cycle Guidelines and complete the Grant Eligibility Checklist. Contact the program officer if you are unsure whether your work fits.

steps.title: Prepare your answers
steps.text: Download the Community Impact Grant Application Worksheet to draft responses offline. The worksheet mirrors every question in the portal.

steps.title: Create or update your portal account
steps.text: New applicants create an organization profile in the CPCF Grant Portal. Returning applicants sign in and confirm that board, budget, and contact information are current.

steps.title: Submit the application
steps.text: Submit the online application, current-year operating budget, and most recent board-approved financial statements by 5:00 p.m. MST on March 12, 2027.

steps.title: Site visit and decision
steps.text: Program staff may schedule a phone call or site visit in April. All applicants are notified of decisions by May 28, 2027.

review_criteria: Alignment with Spring Cycle fields of interest
Clarity of the organization's mission and evidence of community need
Equity: the organization is led by, or meaningfully involves, the communities it serves
Collaboration with other organizations, agencies, or tribal programs

reporting.summary: Grantees submit a brief Community Impact Story Report at the end of the grant period.
items: A short narrative (300–500 words) or photo story describing how the grant strengthened the organization
Number of people served during the grant year
Permission indicating whether CPCF may share the story publicly

contact.name: Elena Brightwater
contact.title: Senior Program Officer, Health & Economic Opportunity

faq.q: We received a Fall 2026 Community Impact Grant. Can we apply in Spring 2027?
faq.a: No. Organizations that received a Community Impact Grant in calendar year 2026 must wait until the 2028 cycles. You may still apply to the Foundation's other funds and to the Shared Giving Catalog.

faq.q: Can a fiscally sponsored project apply?
faq.a: Yes. Include a signed letter from your fiscal sponsor using the Fiscal Sponsor Letter Template. The award tier is based on the project's budget, not the sponsor's.
